standard_prerequisites.name: The pushforward along a closed immersion of ringed spaces is exact, so the derived and the plain pushforward agree
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the proof work with the plain pushforward throughout.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finitely generated cohomology module of a pseudo-coherent complex admits, locally, a surjection from a finite free module onto it
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the map from a shifted free module onto the top cohomology group.

standard_prerequisites.name: In a distinguished triangle, if two terms are pseudo-coherent then so is the third, so cutting off the top cohomology preserves the property
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 3166-3168 and again at proof lines 3170-3175
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the cone is pseudo-coherent and then that the pushed forward complex is pseudo-coherent.

core_obligations: Record that the pushforward is exact so no derived functors are involved, and reduce the forward implication to a local statement at a point of the closed subset, shrinking the ambient space so that the complex is bounded above (proof lines 3151-3159).
Argue by induction on the largest degree p in which the cohomology is nonzero: if p is smaller than the bound there is nothing to prove (proof lines 3157-3159).
In the remaining case choose, after shrinking, a map from a shifted finite free module onto the top cohomology group, using that this cohomology module is of finite type (proof lines 3160-3165).

Form the distinguished triangle with that map and the resulting cone, note that the cone has no cohomology in degrees at least p and is again pseudo-coherent, and apply the induction hypothesis to it (proof lines 3166-3170).

Push the triangle forward, use that the pushforward of the structure sheaf is pseudo-coherent by hypothesis, and apply the two out of three statement for pseudo-coherent complexes in a triangle to conclude that the pushforward of the original complex is pseudo-coherent (proof lines 3170-3176).

Obtain the reverse implication by the same induction argument, where the roles of the complex and its pushforward are exchanged and one uses the surjectivity of the map onto the top cohomology group after pushing forward (proof lines 3177-3221).
proof_roadmap: Exactness of the pushforward and reduction to a local induction on the top degree (proof lines 3151-3159).
Cut off the top cohomology by a distinguished triangle and push it forward (proof lines 3160-3176).
The reverse implication by the exchanged induction (proof lines 3177-3221).
